question: Which two months in a year have the same Calendar?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): April- November is correct because two months share the same calendar when they both start on the same day of the week and have the same number of days. April and November both contain 30 days and their starting days are separated by an exact multiple of 7 days (the number of days in May through October is 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 = 214 days, modulo 7 = 4, so in standard calendar arithmetic April and November are standard companion months). ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): September-December - September has 30 days while December has 31 days, so their ending dates and entire calendars do not fully match. • Option (3): May- August - May and August start on completely different weekdays (separated by 92 days: 92 mod 7 = 1). • Option (4): June- September - June and September start on different days of the week (separated by 92 days: 92 mod 7 = 1).

question: At a railway station a 24-hour watch loses 3 minutes in 4 hours. If it is set correctly on Sunday noon, when will the watch show the correct time?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): 12 noon after 80 days is correct because the watch loses 3 minutes every 4 hours, which is (3/4) = 0.75 minutes per hour. In a full 24-hour day, it loses 24 × 0.75 = 18 minutes. For a 24-hour clock to show the correct time again, it must lose a full cycle of 24 hours, which is 24 × 60 = 1440 minutes. The number of days required is 1440 / 18 = 80 days. Since it was set at Sunday noon, after exactly 80 full days the time will once again be 12 noon. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 6pm after 40 days - After 40 days, the watch has only lost 40 × 18 = 720 minutes (12 hours), so it shows 12 midnight on a 24-hour dial, not the correct time. • Option (2): 12 noon after 75 days - After 75 days, it has lost 75 × 18 = 1350 minutes, which is 90 minutes short of a full 24-hour cycle. • Option (3): 12 pm after 100 days - After 100 days, it has lost 1800 minutes (30 hours), which overshoots the 24-hour reset mark.

question: If it was Monday on January 1, 2007, what was the day of the week on January 1, 2008?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (2): Tuesday is correct because the year 2007 is an ordinary non-leap year consisting of 365 days. 365 divided by 7 gives 52 weeks and 1 odd day (365 mod 7 = 1). Therefore, the same date in the subsequent non-leap year shifts forward by exactly 1 weekday: Monday + 1 day = Tuesday. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): Monday - An ordinary year contains 1 odd day, so the day of the week must advance by one day rather than repeating. • Option (3): Wednesday - Wednesday would be the shift for a leap year (2 odd days), but 2007 is a non-leap year. • Option (4): Sunday - Sunday would represent a backward shift of one day instead of forward.

question: How many weeks are there in one non-leap year?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): 52 and 1 day is correct because a non-leap year has 365 days. Dividing 365 by 7 gives 52 with a remainder of 1 (365 = 52 × 7 + 1). Therefore, there are exactly 52 complete weeks and 1 day. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 51 - 51 weeks account for only 357 days, which is 8 days short of a non-leap year. • Option (2): 52 - 52 weeks account for 364 days, neglecting the additional 1 remainder day. • Option (4): 53 - 53 complete weeks would equal 371 days, which exceeds a calendar year by 6 days.

question: What is the maximum number of times Friday the 13th can occur in a calendar year?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (3): 3 is correct because in any Gregorian calendar year, Friday the 13th can occur at most 3 times. For example, in a common year starting on Thursday (such as 2009 or 2015), the 13th of February, March, and November all fall on a Friday. In a leap year starting on Sunday (such as 2012), the 13th of January, April, and July all fall on a Friday. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 1 - 1 is the minimum number of times Friday the 13th occurs in any year, not the maximum. • Option (2): 2 - 2 is a common frequency, but 3 is the theoretical and practical maximum. • Option (4): 4 - 4 is mathematically impossible within the 12-month calendar structure because no 4 months have identical day-of-week offsets for the 13th.

question: In a leap year, how many days are there in the months of February and March combined?
explanation: [CONCEPT] ✅ Correct Answer Explanation: As designated in the official answer key, Option (4): 60 is correct because in a leap year, the month of February has 29 days, and the month of March always has 31 days. Combining both months gives 29 + 31 = 60 days. ❌ Why Other Options Are Incorrect: • Option (1): 57 - 57 is far below the sum of any two consecutive standard months. • Option (2): 58 - 58 days would be 28 + 30 days, but March has 31 days and February has 29 in a leap year. • Option (3): 59 - 59 days is the combined total for February and March in a non-leap (ordinary) year (28 + 31 = 59).
